report.title: Frontend i18n audit and optimization plan
scope: Static UI strings and accessibility text
Dynamic product, category, brand, review and order data
Translation namespaces, fallback behavior and locale formatting

existingReportContext.result: Locale JSON files are structurally consistent across 9 languages.
existingReportContext.limitation: That report does not validate frontend key usage, runtime namespace loading, hard-coded JSX text, accessibility labels or dynamic API data.

architectureFindings.problem: Translation values are not centralized in the frontend. Static values are split across backend locale files by language and namespace.
architectureFindings.impact: The split supports lazy loading, but makes key discovery, duplicate detection and cross-locale review harder.
architectureFindings.optimization: Keep locale and namespace files as the runtime source, then generate one machine-readable manifest and validate all namespaces in CI. Do not merge every namespace into one runtime bundle.

architectureFindings.problem: Translation keys are referenced throughout TSX files rather than being discoverable from a single typed registry.
architectureFindings.impact: It is easy to introduce a missing key, an incorrect namespace or a key collision without a build-time error.
architectureFindings.optimization: Extract t(...) usages into a report, validate each key against the selected namespace files, and standardize calls to t(key, namespace).

architectureFindings.problem: The frontend messages module is empty and deprecated.
architectureFindings.impact: There is no local typed fallback catalog when the translation API and IndexedDB cache are unavailable.
architectureFindings.optimization: Generate a small fallback catalog from the default locale during build, or make the backend fallback endpoint the explicit single fallback source. Avoid maintaining a second hand-written catalog.

architectureFindings.problem: Static labels, spec labels and dynamic entity translations are stored in different systems.
architectureFindings.impact: The same label can have different fallback behavior and validation rules depending on which translation path renders it.
architectureFindings.optimization: Define a translation ownership matrix: static UI in locale namespaces, specification keys in one shared catalog, and product/review content in dynamic translation storage. Expose consistent APIs and fallback rules for all three.

issues.problem: Product specification labels can render raw keys such as processor, ram or screenSize.
issues.rootCause: specLabels is prepared by the product page but SpecsTable receives only specs.
issues.impact: Translated specification labels are ignored in the full specification tab.
issues.recommendedFix: Pass specLabels to SpecsTable and resolve each key through specLabels before using the canonical key as fallback.

issues.problem: Visible English strings remain hard-coded in the coupon form and admin loading wrappers.
issues.recommendedFix: Replace Currency, Select currency and Loading... with namespaced translation keys.

issues.impact: Backend English messages, internal error codes or technical details can bypass the selected locale and leak to users.
issues.recommendedFix: Map stable API error codes to namespaced translation keys. Use a generic localized fallback for unknown errors and keep raw messages in logs only.

issues.problem: Review translation uses a separate API base URL and localhost fallback.
issues.impact: Review translation can fail in production when NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is absent or points to a different origin.
issues.recommendedFix: Use the same /api proxy convention as the other translation requests and keep the API origin configuration in one place.

issues.problem: Missing translations return the key path itself.
issues.impact: Users can see values such as loading or filter_no_products_found when a namespace has not loaded or the translation service is unavailable.
issues.recommendedFix: Use the default locale or a generated fallback catalog before returning a key. Expose missing-key telemetry for development and monitoring.

issues.problem: Product cards depend on localized API responses and do not have the same translation fallback as product detail.
issues.impact: Listing and detail pages can display different languages or untranslated product content when an API translation is missing.
issues.recommendedFix: Create one shared product display-localization adapter for name, brand, description, specs and specLabels. Keep API data as the primary source and apply deterministic fallback order.

issues.problem: Dynamic brand data is passed to the translation function as if it were a translation key.
issues.impact: A brand can collide with a UI key or appear as a raw key when no translation exists.
issues.recommendedFix: Render the brand value directly after API localization. Use t(...) only for the no_brand fallback.

issues.problem: Ratings use toFixed(1), and several date callers do not use the shared Intl locale mapping.
issues.impact: Decimal separators and date conventions are not guaranteed to match the active locale.
issues.recommendedFix: Centralize number, rating, currency and date formatting with getIntlLocale(locale) and reuse the formatters everywhere.

issues.problem: Several icon-only controls have no translated accessible name.
issues.recommendedFix: Add namespaced aria-label values for controls and a title for the map iframe. Use role=dialog and aria-modal for quick view.

principles: Preserve locale/namespace splitting for runtime performance.
Keep one owner for each translation category.
Make missing keys detectable before deployment.
Never use user-facing raw API errors as translated UI text.
Keep dynamic domain data separate from static UI labels.

phases.name: Stabilize runtime behavior
actions: Replace remaining admin hard-coded English strings.
Unify review translation with the /api proxy.
Add a default-locale fallback before returning a key path.
Map raw API errors to translation keys.

phases.name: Create a translation contract
actions: Define a namespace registry with owner and allowed usage area.
Generate a manifest of all keys from backend locale JSON files.
Extract frontend t(...) calls and validate key plus namespace pairs.
Detect duplicate keys and missing locale values in CI.
Define ownership for static UI, spec labels and dynamic entity translations.

phases.name: Unify presentation helpers
actions: Create one product localization adapter shared by cards, search, quick view and detail.
Create shared Intl formatters for rating, quantity, currency and date.
Normalize category and brand values when the API returns either a localized string or a locale map.
Add translated accessible names to all icon-only controls.

phases.name: Monitor quality
actions: Log missing translation keys only in development and monitoring channels.
Track namespace load failures and fallback usage.
Add an automated smoke test for each supported locale on the main storefront routes.

acceptanceCriteria: No visible English hard-code remains in supported storefront or admin routes.
No product specification tab displays a canonical key when a localized spec label exists.
No user-facing error or toast renders a raw backend message by default.
Missing translation values fall back to a localized source instead of exposing a key path.
Frontend key usage and backend locale files are validated in CI.
All icon-only controls and embedded frames have an accessible localized name.
Rating, date and currency formatting follows the active locale.
